title: A live frog has floated in a magnet
body: In 1997 Andre Geim's group floated a frog in a 16-tesla magnet, exploiting water's weak diamagnetism: the field slightly repels the frog's own water. Nothing was harmed; the frog reportedly seemed fine. The experiment won an Ig Nobel, after which Geim also won a real Nobel for graphene, a unique double.
